To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fluoroscopic‐based tumor tracking system for the superconducting rotating carbon‐ion gantry is feasible.
the tumor tracking system was commissioned and validated in a superconductive rotating gantry.

(i) the fluoroscopic‐based markerless tumor tracking method is feasible for real‐time tumor tracking in superconducting rotating‐gantry carbon‐ion pencil‐beam scanning treatment; (ii) the accuracy of the tumor tracking method was comparable to the accuracy of the current marker‐based tumor tracking method; and (iii) the fluoroscopic imaging dose was negligible.

developing an efficient and accurate method for tracking the tumor position during the carbon‐ion beam delivery.
the development of an integrated, real‐time tumor tracking system for carbon ion radiotherapy.
